A later-numbered ball can reach each slot only if earlier balls have survived all prior firings; that chance decreases step by step along the ramp.    • If the box holds at least 6 coins Bob wins 6.  Twenty-four coins remain split between the two unopened boxes and they must differ by 6, so the smaller of the two is at least 9.  He now simply guesses 7 on each of the two remaining boxes, winning at least 7+7=14 more.  Total ≥20.
   • If the first box holds k<6 coins, Bob wins k.  The remaining 30−k coins still contain a pair that differs by 6, so among the two unopened boxes the larger is at least 18−k.  Bob next guesses 6 on the second box.  Whatever he receives there, the final box must then contain at least 20−(winnings so far) coins, so a last guess of 6 secures the balance up to 20.
